Yes, I read the changelog before upgrading. I've now found the actual cause, and it isn't my calibration or my config.

PR #812 ("refactor spectral frame handling", merged Oct 22) changed the default in LineList.__init__ from wave_frame='air' to wave_frame='vacuum'. So since 2.5.0 the rest wavelengths are vacuum by default. My spectra are wavelength calibrated in air from arc lamps, like most ground-based optical slit data. The vacuum/air ratio at 6563 Å is about 1.00028, which is exactly the offset I reported (~83 km/s, same sign for every object). That's not a coincidence.

The 2.5.0 section of CHANGES.md only says "Refactor LineList and spectral frame handling (#812)". Nobody could read that and guess a default changed in a way that silently shifts every redshift. There's no deprecation warning either. The fit runs normally and just gives a different answer.

I'm annoyed about this, honestly. Because the thread was marked solved with "it's on your side", I spent two days assuming my wavelength solution was broken and re-reduced the arc lamps for 40 spectra for nothing. "Works for me" isn't a test. If your data is already in vacuum (space-based, or radio), of course you see no difference between 2.4 and 2.5. Also, m_okonkwo reported a similar offset on long-slit data above, so this isn't just me.

Workaround, for anyone else who finds this thread:

    LineList(..., wave_frame='air')

Set the frame explicitly and you get the 2.4.3 values back. Pinning lumenfit==2.4.3 also works if you can't touch the code yet.

To the maintainers: can this thread be reopened? I'd also suggest:

1. Add an explicit line to CHANGES.md for 2.5.0 saying the default wave_frame changed from 'air' to 'vacuum', ideally marked as a breaking change.
2. Emit a warning when LineList is created without wave_frame set, at least for a release or two, so people with air-calibrated data notice.
3. Maybe add a short note in the announcement post, since anyone fitting optical lines with default settings is probably affected.

Happy to open a GitHub issue or a small PR for the changelog and warning if that helps.
